title: eGain Introduces AI KnowledgeOps to Power Trustworthy AI From Living Knowledge
body_markdown:
## New industry framework keeps AI answers accurate as customer needs, products, and regulations change


**Sunnyvale, CA (October 13, 2026):** eGain Corporation (NASDAQ:[EGAN](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/egan) ), today introduced[AI KnowledgeOps](https://www.egain.com/ai-knowledge-ops/) , an industry framework for keeping enterprise knowledge accurate and ready for AI as a business and its industry keep changing. It gives organizations an ongoing way to make sure the answers and actions AI delivers are consistent and correct, so companies can rely on AI across more of their customer and employee interactions. Alongside the framework, eGain introduced four new capabilities that make it faster and easier for teams to run AI KnowledgeOps every day.


### Trustworthy AI Starts with Knowledge


AI makes it easy to produce an answer that sounds right whether or not it is. When an AI agent gets an answer or an action wrong, the business pays for it in a poor customer experience, a higher cost to fix, and compliance exposure in regulated industries. AI models can only be as reliable as the knowledge content they draw from.


Based on eGain’s work with enterprises across banking, insurance, and healthcare, around 80 percent of a knowledge base’s value tends to come from about 20 percent of its content. That content is often scattered across several systems and buried under duplicates, outdated articles, and guidance written for a different audience. Few organizations have an ongoing way to find it, verify it, and keep it current as their products, policies, and regulations change. Knowledge starts going stale the day a new product launches, a rate changes, or a regulation is updated, and AI ends up repeating whatever it was last given.


### The AI KnowledgeOps Process


AI KnowledgeOps runs as a continuous loop. It starts with what a business already has – the conversations happening across every channel and the content spread across its systems – and uses both to uncover the questions that customers are asking and which topics matter most to the business.


Those questions are checked against existing content to find what’s missing or incomplete, so teams can close the highest-impact gaps first. Knowledge is tagged and mapped to the products, policies, and rules it relates to so AI can find the right answer for the right person. Answers are then tested against real customer questions and refined until they are satisfactory, with governance built in throughout. One approved source powers every AI agent and channel, with everything personalized for each customer. How each answer, agent, and AI model performs feeds back into the process, along with relevant updates to products, policies, and regulations, so knowledge stays accurate as the business changes and customers and employees get answers and actions they can trust.


### New Capabilities That Make AI KnowledgeOps Easier


Four new eGain capabilities help teams drive a more efficient and accurate AI Knowledge Ops process.


[WYCA](https://www.egain.com/wyca/) **(What Your Customers Ask)** is a free tool that reads customer conversations across channels and groups together the many ways people ask the same question. It then shows which questions matter most to the business because they matter most to customers. In just a few clicks, teams can analyze all their conversations to see what knowledge they need and where to put their effort. WYCA runs inside an organization’s firewall, so customer data stays secure and private inside the company’s own environment.


[eGain Knowledge Graphs](https://www.egain.com/knowledge-graphs/) give AI agents a map and a shared vocabulary of how a business operates. Teams can automatically model the topics that matter, like products, policies, and fees, and link each one to the trusted articles that explain them. When a customer question draws on several sources at once, an AI agent can query the graph and give a complete, accurate answer in fewer steps. Every graph gets the same version control, auditing, and governance as the rest of the eGain platform.


[eGain Genie](https://www.egain.com/genie/) is a conversational AI agent built into all eGain products. Knowledge authors and knowledge engineers can ask Genie in plain language to write multiple articles, create reports, or build agentic workflows. One request replaces hours of work across editors, report builders, and workflow designers. Genie follows the organization’s own templates, style guides, and policies every time. It also handles large jobs, like turning training videos into articles or updating hundreds of articles at once.


[eGain kForge](https://www.egain.com/kforge/) is a services accelerator that connects every content source and eliminates the painful migration typically associated with getting content ready for AI at scale. Ready-made connectors move content into eGain once or keep it in sync. A library of agentic actions allows teams to transform content, including converting documents with differing metadata and formats, consolidating duplicates across thousands of articles, and extracting knowledge graphs automatically. A subject matter expert can review anything considered high risk, and every change is traced back to its source. Companies get one accurate, consistent version of their knowledge without a long manual migration project.


“The first thing every executive wants to know before putting AI in front of customers is whether it will get the answer right and take the right action, and both come down to the knowledge behind it,” said Ashu Roy, CEO of eGain. “AI KnowledgeOps gives companies a repeatable process to make sure it does, even as their business keeps changing. We’ve spent more than 25 years helping enterprises manage knowledge, and the organizations seeing real results from AI are the ones that treat knowledge as an ongoing practice. The capabilities we’re introducing today make that practice faster and easier to maintain, so teams can bring their content together, see what customers actually need, and keep every answer and action current.”
